title: Grand Abolisher - mtg.wtf
claim: Grand Abolisher prevents opponents from casting spells during its controller's turn and from activating abilities of artifacts, creatures, or enchantments during that turn.
cross_check: current Oracle mirror; production use must rederive from pinned Scryfall bulk/CR

title: Defense Grid - mtg.wtf
claim: Defense Grid taxes every spell by three generic mana unless that spell is cast during its controller's turn.
cross_check: current Oracle mirror; production use must rederive from pinned Scryfall bulk/CR

title: Replacement for Grand Abolisher? - TappedOut
claim: Players explicitly discuss Defense Grid as a replacement-like option for Grand Abolisher when the desired job is making opposing interaction on the pilot's turn harder.
cross_check: mechanisms differ materially: prohibition versus spell tax; Grand Abolisher also covers specified activated abilities

title: The First Sliver deck primer - MTGGoldfish
claim: A Food Chain primer describes Plunge into Darkness as functioning like a very large Dig Through Time in the deck's card-finding role.
cross_check: Oracle differs in payment, depth, number retained, and residual-card destination
conflicts: similar wording appears on multiple deck-hosting platforms and may share lineage, so those mirrors are not treated as independent corroboration

title: Plunge into Darkness - mtg.wtf
claim: One mode of Plunge into Darkness lets its controller pay any amount of life, inspect that many cards from the top of the library, keep one in hand, and exile the rest.
cross_check: current Oracle mirror

title: Dig Through Time - mtg.wtf
claim: Dig Through Time looks at the top seven cards, puts two into hand, and puts the rest on the bottom; delve changes payment resources rather than that selection result.
cross_check: current Oracle mirror

title: Ramp in Commander - EDHREC
claim: EDHREC defines ramp functionally as increasing mana available in a turn above ordinary on-curve production, and explicitly groups land ramp, mana dorks, mana rocks, enchantment acceleration, cost reducers, and other accelerants under that parent job.
cross_check: community/editorial taxonomy, not CR truth
conflicts: community discussions disagree about whether one-shot rituals should be called ramp

title: How to Build a Commander Deck - EDHREC
claim: Commander deckbuilding guidance uses broad functional categories such as ramp, card advantage/velocity, interaction, tutors, board wipes, and graveyard hate, while allowing a card to contribute to more than one role.
cross_check: community/editorial taxonomy, not canonical mechanics

title: Mechanical Memories - Bored of Board Wipes? - EDHREC
claim: The term board wipe is used as a broad functional category for effects that clear a substantial section of the battlefield, with acknowledged fuzzy boundaries rather than a single mechanical template.
cross_check: community term; do not infer a specific zone-change verb

title: EDHREC Guide to cEDH Stax
claim: Stax is used as a strategic umbrella for effects that constrain opponents' ability to act or efficiently execute their game plan, spanning multiple mechanical implementations.
cross_check: strategic label; must never be imported as direct Oracle fact
conflicts: boundary with tax, hatebear, prison, and control terminology varies by community

title: Too-Specific Top 10 - Commander Outlet - EDHREC
claim: Sacrifice outlet is used for repeatable or readily available ways to sacrifice one's own permanents, especially creatures, often as enabling infrastructure rather than as the payoff itself.
cross_check: community role term; cost, repeatability, object scope, and output remain separate coordinates

title: Technically Playable - Tura Kennerud, Skyknight - EDHREC
claim: Cantrip is used for a cheap spell that replaces itself by drawing a card, which is card flow/velocity rather than net card advantage by itself.
cross_check: community term; exact cost ceiling is not stable enough to canonicalize here

title: Top 10 Game Changer Alternatives - EDHREC
claim: Cyclonic Rift is compared to other mass-interaction or board-reset effects while the article also stresses that cards doing parts of its job are not exact replacements.
cross_check: supports graded similarity rather than binary replacement equivalence

title: What if Commander Had Sideboards? - EDHREC
claim: Rest in Peace and Soul-Guide Lantern are both treated as graveyard-hate options even though one is persistent replacement-style denial and the other includes one-shot graveyard exile.
cross_check: same role family, different persistence and coverage

title: Rest in Peace - mtg.wtf
claim: Rest in Peace exiles graveyards on entry and replaces future card/token graveyard movement with exile.
cross_check: current Oracle mirror

title: Dark Ritual - mtg.wtf
claim: Dark Ritual is one-shot mana production: it adds three black mana when the instant resolves.
cross_check: current Oracle mirror

title: r/EDH ramp terminology discussions sampled 2026-09-12
claim: Commander players disagree on whether one-shot rituals belong inside the word ramp: some include any net mana acceleration, while others reserve ramp for durable/repeatable acceleration and call rituals fast or burst mana.
cross_check: usage conflict deliberately preserved; no majority rule inferred

title: Sphere of Resistance - mtg.wtf
claim: Sphere of Resistance makes all spells cost one generic mana more, including its controller's spells.
cross_check: current Oracle mirror

title: Faithless Looting - mtg.wtf
claim: Faithless Looting draws two then discards two for its controller, with flashback; it is self-filtering rather than a table-wide hand reset.
cross_check: current Oracle mirror

title: Exploration - mtg.wtf
claim: Exploration grants permission to play one additional land on each of its controller's turns; it does not itself search for or move a land from the library.
cross_check: current Oracle mirror

title: Path E M2 frozen evaluation panel
claim: A human-frozen pre-existing panel names correct neighbours for Rampant Growth, Beast Within, Reanimate, and Reliquary Tower and treats Sol Ring and Grand Abolisher as controls against fabricated semantic evidence.
cross_check: repository blob-pinned transcription; not semantic authority

title: Accepted S9 retrieval implementation
claim: S9 admits a candidate only when anchor and candidate share at least one ACTIVE axis; zero shared ACTIVE axes is structural non-discoverability, and ordering is shared-axis count then specificity/cardinality with deterministic tie-breaking.
cross_check: accepted implementation head 9f92039eb9c7132a351576c31472eb30a2957a67

title: M2/S9 evaluation measurement
claim: In the frozen panel, S9 discovered only part of the named-correct set and often produced very large tie blocks; Grand Abolisher had zero ACTIVE memberships and therefore zero candidates without fabricated evidence.
cross_check: measurement evidence only; must not be converted into relevance ground truth
